angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 785,445 km at 35.43 pc = 0.3 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 28.2210 +/- 0.0185 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 35.43 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.129 +/- 0.013 solar radii from DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract): 785,445 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.05 +/- 0.044 solar masses from DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6081 +/- 60 K from DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-60779.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.354, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 60779 (pscomppars): spectral type G1 V, from DiTomasso et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 60779 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.12 dex, from DiTomasso et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 60779 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.19479, from DiTomasso et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 3060787930730737920, flags_flame 00: age_flame 6.425854 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 5.5045614 to 7.34692)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 60779 (pscomppars): rotation period 19 d, from DiTomasso et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 60779 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3 km/s, from DiTomasso et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.129 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.998. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
